key_insight: A decision model can handle some structured clinical tasks at much lower cost than large language models, but its performance depends strongly on how the task is framed.
clinical_relevance: In precision oncology workflows, decision models could help offload low-risk structured tasks such as mortality estimation, triage questions, and staging, reserving LLMs for harder or uncertain cases.
method: Compared Jev with five flagship LLMs on three clinical tasks: mortality risk, Choosing Wisely-style categorical decisions, and ordinal colon cancer staging.
Tested standard LLM-style prompts versus developer-recommended input changes, including added medical context and task decomposition.
Evaluated a hybrid workflow using Jev only for fully confident staging predictions and LLMs for the remaining cases.
evidence_signal: With standard inputs, Jev underperformed LLMs on all tasks, but tailored prompting raised staging accuracy from 45.4% to 85.8%, and a hybrid approach reduced flagship LLM costs by 33-44% while remaining non-inferior.
watch_item: The system still depends on confidence calibration and careful task design, since incorrect low-confidence or poorly framed outputs could limit safe real-world deployment.
paper_title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
